profile.name: Gookhee Shin
profile.headline: Industrial and Systems Engineering student working across optimization, bioinformatics, manufacturing systems, and social-impact technology.
profile.about: I am an undergraduate student in Industrial and Systems Engineering at KAIST, with a double major in Business and Technology Management. My work connects optimization, data analysis, biomedical systems, manufacturing innovation, and education technology. I am especially interested in turning uncertain real-world problems into measurable decision-making frameworks that can create practical value for healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and learning opportunities.

education.degree: Candidate for BEng in Industrial and Systems Engineering
education.minor: Candidate for BEng in Business and Technology Management, Double Major

items.name: Listeney, AI-Powered Language Habit Correction Platform
bullets: Founded Listeney to reduce opportunity gaps in interviews, presentations, and admissions by objectively diagnosing users' speaking habits through speech-to-text and natural-language-processing technologies.

Led problem definition, product planning, scoring design, IR materials, and investor pitching; designed a six-category feedback system covering grammar, vocabulary, spacing, punctuation, fluency, and pronunciation estimation.
Rebuilt the team after three initial members left during MVP development by recruiting an app developer from KAIST Financial Analysis Club and reorganizing milestones around core functions.
Presented IR pitches to 17 venture investors, including Zero-to-One Partners, IBK Venture Capital, and Blue Point Partners.

Received the Korea Artificial Intelligence Software Industry Association Chairman's Award at the 2025 SW Talent Festival, hosted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and organized by IITP and the SW-Centered University Council.
Received the Silver Prize at Culture-Tech Startup Challenge 2025, organized by the KAIST Graduate School of Culture Technology.

items.name: 2025 Global Entrepreneurship Summer School (GESS)
bullets: Selected as a KAIST fellow and developed an AI-driven digital-nomad startup proposal with an international, cross-disciplinary team.
Completed lectures, mentoring sessions, business-model workshops, and IR pitch preparation focused on venture scalability and global market strategy.

items.name: KAIST Financial Analysis Club (KFAC)
bullets: Led equity research and valuation projects on Samsung Biologics and Amorepacific, combining industry analysis with DCF and comparable-company valuation.
Analyzed ADC, CDMO, biosimilar, and cosmetics markets; built financial models based on pipeline assumptions, market growth, and future cash-flow scenarios.
Earned 1st place in the Spring 2024 Time Folio IVY Club competition and 3rd place in the Fall 2024 competition.

items.name: DAIM LABS, Prof. Young-Jae Jang Laboratory
bullets: Developing a manufacturing process innovation project within DAIM LABS, focusing on Automated Material Handling System (AMHS) simulation.
Interested in modeling material-flow bottlenecks, dispatching logic, and throughput improvement in semiconductor and advanced manufacturing systems.

items.name: Prof. Young-Suk Lee Laboratory
items.role: Undergraduate Researcher, Bioinformatics and Organoid Quality Evaluation
bullets: Presented the poster "Organoid-Tissue Similarity Quantification for Quality Evaluation" at the 2025 IE Frontier Undergraduate Poster Competition.
Developed a quantitative framework for organoid-tissue similarity using single-cell RNA-seq data, PCA-space distance metrics, and linear-programming-based minimum-cost matching.
Validated the metric by comparing high- and low-quality colon organoids against native colon and liver tissue references, supporting reproducible quality evaluation in biomanufacturing.
Received the Top Excellence Award for translating qualitative biomedical evaluation into an engineering metric.
Conducted eye-organoid single-cell analysis, including GEO data retrieval, FASTQC quality control, Cell Ranger alignment, R-based downstream analysis, and journal-club discussions.

items.name: KAIST Industrial and Systems Engineering Student Council
bullets: Coordinated student-facing programs and communication across department members, supporting academic, community, and student-welfare initiatives.

items.name: KAIST Science Outreach Program (KSOP)
bullets: Taught and mentored middle-school students preparing for science high-school admissions through KAIST's flagship outreach program for underrepresented STEM talent.
Designed a preparation track for scientific reasoning, problem solving, interview structure, and personalized academic coaching; supported two students admitted to science high schools.

items.name: KAIST Cyber Gifted Education Center
bullets: Provided online STEM tutoring and feedback to gifted students, strengthening learners' problem-solving processes and academic communication.

items.name: KAIST Overseas Volunteer Program, Santo Lukas High School
bullets: Planned and delivered in-person educational outreach programs, adapting lesson content during flood-related disruptions to preserve learning opportunities.
Organized lesson design, teaching demonstrations, team rehearsals, and cultural-exchange activities with local students.

items.name: Intermediate Speaking & Listening, Prof. John Looney
bullets: Assisted English presentation and discussion courses by grading assignments, supporting class operations, and providing feedback on clarity, delivery, and spoken fluency.
